transcript:
Header: 2027-06-30 15:00 PDT | Duration: ~45m | Attendees: Lena Park (Redwood AE), Marcus Chen (Redwood SE), Aisha Khan (Novapay Head of Platform), Diego Ramos (ML Eng), Priya Singh (SRE)

[00:00] Lena Park: hey everyone, thanks for joining. quick agenda - review the latest throughput numbers, dig into tuning knobs (continuous batching, concurrency, queueing) and decide next benchmark and next steps. tia.

[00:22] Aisha Khan: yep thanks lena. we got the report you sent yester - the throughput spike looked promising. main ask from our side is we need predictable p95 latency under 350ms for the payments flows, and we need to understand cost delta if we move from hosted to dedicated.

[00:45] Marcus Chen: cool. quick recap - last run was single-node with continuous batching on by default, we used the 8k token model variant you asked for, average request size ~480 tokens, and we saw about 420 rps peak with median latency around 140ms but p95 touching 380-420ms during bursts. so p95 is a little high.

[01:10] Diego Ramos: i remember on our side we saw occasional 500ms spikes, mainly around end-of-minute bursts when many sessions align. seems like queueing/backpressure issue?

[01:32] Marcus Chen: yeah that matches. continuous batching helps aggregate short requests to fill batches and increases throughput/cost efficiency, but it can add a small waiting window which hurts tail latency during synchronous bursts. There's a tradeoff knob: batch timeout and max batch size, and you can set concurrency targets to reduce the queue length at high load.

[01:58] Priya Singh: can you remind me what our SLOs are for throughput vs latency? we need the correct knobs to avoid breaking SLAs.

[02:10] Aisha Khan: SLO is p95 < 350ms for our critical auth/settlement path. Average cost target is under $0.0009 per token processed if possible - that's a soft number.

[02:28] Lena Park: ok so objectives clear. Marcus, can you walk through the tuning options and what changed from the last run?

[02:36] Marcus Chen: sure. options we tweaked: continuous batching enabled with 5ms max delay, max_batch_size of 128, and concurrency target of 48. On the single-node run that gave us high avg throughput but the p95 slippage. For the next run we propose: increase concurrency target to 64 on a 2-node cluster, raise max_batch_size slightly to 160, and reduce batch timeout to 3ms to shave tail. we'll also enable prefix/KV caching for repeated prompts which should reduce effective token load for warm sessions.

[03:20] Diego Ramos: with KW cache - you mean KV cache for the transformer attention states? does that reduce token generation cost for multi-turn?

[03:30] Marcus Chen: yes, kv cache reuse for continuing chats reduces compute per token after the initial prompt. for your flows that reuse a standard header/consent text it'll help a lot. but not all flows can use it.

[03:45] Aisha Khan: what about queueing? i.e., when we target 64 concurrency, do we risk more queued requests and higher tail?

[03:55] Marcus Chen: good question. there's two ways to think about it: target concurrency tells the router/launcher how many concurrent requests to keep in flight per model shard. Higher concurrency can increase throughput but also increases variance if the batch buildup is uneven. To control queueing we use two levers: 1) admission control (a small queue length + immediate reject/fallback to a cheaper model) 2) backpressure signals to clients. For the POC we'll simulate admission control with a small request queue and config fallback to a smaller quantized variant if queue depth hits threshold.

[04:45] Priya Singh: fallback to a quantized variant - is output quality consistent? we're sensitive in payments flows to hallucinations.

[04:55] Marcus Chen: qualitatively yes for short generation tasks; we calibrate evaluation sets against your prompt bank. Redwood Optimize can produce suggested quantization profiles and run regtests to ensure quality doesn't regress significantly. We'll share the evaluation diff.

[05:18] Lena Park: do you have numbers for expected cost changes when moving from hosted to Dedicated? Aisha asked for delta.

[05:26] Marcus Chen: estimated - on our hosted plan, your current run cost ~ $0.11 per 1k tokens because of multi-tenant overhead and lower batch fullness. With Dedicated and tuned continuous batching + higher concurrency, you could drop near-term unit cost to $0.07-$0.08 per 1k tokens depending on utilization. The biggest wins are batching and caching. We'll put a worksheet together with ranges.

[05:56] Diego Ramos: interesting. what's the ops tradeoff? we want predictable throughput during month-end spikes.

[06:05] Marcus Chen: Dedicated gives reserved GPU pools and autoscaling policies you control. For spikes we recommend a small burst pool and a canary fallback region. Also can set automatic cap on concurrency to avoid noisy neighbor effect internal to your own pool if you share capacity across teams.

[06:30] Aisha Khan: Security-wise we need to see SOC2 and KMS integration doc. Also SSO for RBAC.

[06:40] Lena Park: yep i'll send the redacted SOC2 snapshot and KMS integration guide after the call.

[06:48] Marcus Chen: back to tuning - we propose the next benchmark to be 2 nodes (same model), continuous batching on with 3ms timeout, max_batch_size 160, concurrency target 64, and admission queue limit at 128 requests. We'll capture median/p95/p99 latencies and token/sec. Also run a run with batching off to compare.

[07:20] Diego Ramos: can you also add a run that simulates end-of-minute traffic alignment? that's where we saw the p99 spikes.

[07:26] Marcus Chen: yes we'll simulate bursty traffic patterns (diurnal + aligned bursts).

[07:33] Priya Singh: what telemetry will you surface? we need per-route token counts, p95 latency, queue depth, batch sizes, and cost per token.

[07:42] Marcus Chen: Redwood Console will show per-route breakdowns, batch fullness, token cost and traces. we'll throw together a dashboard link with the runs.

[07:50] Aisha Khan: okay good. one worry - we use GCP region us-west1 with private VPC. How does Private deployment differ? If we go Dedicated but still need VPC peering?

[08:02] Lena Park: Dedicated is still managed by Redwood but can be deployed into your VPC in a Private setup or we can do an interconnect depending on compliance. We'll include network options in the pricing sheet.

[08:15] Marcus Chen: technical note - for private VPC, there's slightly higher network egress, that can add a few ms but usually negligible for local regions. We'll measure latency from your egress point in the bench.

[08:30] Diego Ramos: ok. any quick wins we can apply right now to reduce p95 without adding nodes?

[08:37] Marcus Chen: yes - reduce batch timeout from 5ms to 3ms and set a soft concurrency target bump to 56; enable prefix caching for repeated prompts; and configure admission control to shed to quantized fallback at 95% queue. These changes often reduce p95 by 15-25% on single-node runs.

[09:00] Aisha Khan: do it. and please annotate logs so we can see request ids.

[09:08] Marcus Chen: will do. Also we'll produce a short eval comparing your top 50 prompt set across the main model and the quantized variant so you can judge quality.

[09:22] Lena Park: logistics - Marcus, can you run the 2-node benchmark and upload by Friday? Aisha, can you share the request histogram and token distribution?

[09:32] Aisha Khan: yes i'll get the histogram by Friday morning.

[09:36] Diego Ramos: one more Q - queueing strategy: do you support per-customer queue limits in the router? we want per-route caps.

[09:44] Marcus Chen: yes per-route caps and per-customer quotas. we'll show the config snippet.

[09:52] Priya Singh: for canarying, can you run 10% traffic to the quantized fallback to compare production metrics?

[09:59] Marcus Chen: yes canary config is straightforward, we can set 10% traffic funnel.

[10:05] Lena Park: wrap up quick - recap next steps. Marcus to run 2-node with config above; Lena to send pricing and SOC2 and KMS docs; Aisha to share production histograms; schedule side-by-side latency run vs competitor next week.

[10:24] Aisha Khan: sounds good, thanks all.

[10:30] Lena Park: thanks everyone. we'll follow up in email with links and the benchmark artifacts.

[10:40] End of recording.
